nodes.natural_language: Restate the target claim: the equation sum_{k=1}^n k i^k = 48 + 49i holds precisely when n = 97.

The closed-form formula for the arithmetico-geometric series S = sum_{k=1}^n k r^k is S = r(1 - (n+1)r^n + n r^{n+1}) / (1-r)^2 for r 
eq 1.
Substitute r = i into the closed form and simplify using i^4 = 1 and (1-i)^2 = -2i to obtain an explicit expression depending on n mod 4.
For n ≡ 1 (mod 4) the powers of i evaluate to i^n = i and i^{n+1} = -1, yielding the real and imaginary parts Re(S) = (n+1)/2 and Im(S) = -(n-1)/2.
Set n = 97 = 4·24 + 1. Then Re(S) = 49 and Im(S) = -48, so S = 48 + 49i, confirming the target equation.
Let S = sum_{k=1}^n k i^k. The closed-form formula sum k r^k = r(1-(n+1)r^n + n r^{n+1}) / (1-r)^2 with r = i yields an explicit expression for S.
Because i^4 = 1, the summands k i^k are periodic of period 4, so it suffices to evaluate the partial sums according to the residue class of n modulo 4.
nodes.statement: i^4=1 ⇒ periodicity of period 4 for summands; evaluate S by n mod 4
